basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: The shared backbone for anything that happened: one shape for time, place, participants, causality and evidence.
Can record that something did not happen, and keeps records made in error as such.
Separates event time, observation time and recording time.

may: Record an occurrence with evidence and stated uncertainty.
Link occurrences by part-whole or causal relations with evidence.
Correct a record by appending a correction.
mustNot: State a cause as fact without evidence.
Assign intent or blame; that belongs to the act model and to people.
Drop stated uncertainty when copying a record.
requiresHuman: Merging records that may describe different occurrences.

considerations: Event records about people (incidents, accidents) can stigmatize; keep facts separate from judgement.
Negative assertions and corrections protect people from false records.
affectedParties: People and organizations taking part in events
Investigators and the public relying on records

owners.steward: The recording authority for each kind of event (operator, registry, investigator) owns its records.

items: An occurrence record has a type, a time with precision, a setting, participants and sources.
Duplicate events from multiple observers counted twice.
Clock and time zone errors changing order of events.
